title: BOSCH GWS8-45 4-1/2 Inch 7.5 Amp Angle Grinder with Lock-On Switch, Lightweight Design, and Durable Protection Guard for Metal and Concrete Grinding
description:
About this item
COMPACT: Weighing only 4.2 lbs., the Bosch GWS8-45 Angle Grinder is lightweight and compact. Its slender grip circumference allows users to work comfortably for longer.
POWER: The angle grinder features a powerful 7.5-amp motor to produce 11,000 no-load rpm for professional cutting and grinding applications.
ERGONOMIC: With its slim-grip design, the GWS8-45 angle grinder provides outstanding user comfort. Its two-position side handle allows for greater control and utility.
PROTECTION: The grinder also provides directed air flow to divert dust from vital components for enhanced durability and longer tool life. The burst-protection guard provides quick adjustments for user security.
LONGEVITY: Bosch's Service Minder brush system shuts off the tool when preventative maintenance is required, extending overall tool life.

reviews_5s:
I bought this to cut some ~1/8" steel. In particular, this rack:

https://www.amazon.com/dp/B002RYYY7C?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details

The two rows of holes on each post are in line with each other so the rear set needs to be cut off. Not knowing that before I bought that rack, I bought this grinder to do the cutting. I was shocked to find that the manual claims that this grinder cannot be used for cut-off applications, because it doesn't say that anywhere on the Amazon page, or even on Bosch's website, unless you download the manual. However, other manufacturers such as Makita offer similar-sized grinders with the same or lesser specs that claim to support cut-off work, so I figured why not give it a shot. And sure enough, it works just fine. Just don't lay into it too hard and let the disc do the work. Also, wear adequate PPE and a dust mask or respirator, it generates tons of particles and stinks as the disc wears.

Other 4.5" Bosch grinders claim to support cut-off applications, but it seems that Bosch has discontinued the "optional" cut-off guard, and finding guards for other brands of 4.5" grinders seemed equally challenging at this price point. It would appear that most people just toss a cut off disc in there and go, using the included "Type 27" guard that comes stock with this and any other brand of entry-level grinder. User beware, and be careful, but there are loads of videos on YouTube showing people using grinders to cut metal with Type 27 guards installed.

Installing a Type 1 (flat) disc doesn't leave a lot of clearance with the included guard though, so I opted for a Type 27 cutoff wheel. This has the depressed center like the included grinding wheel, and offers better clearance. The one I got (Norton Blue Fire) says to use it with Type 27 guards, which happens to be what's included with this grinder. Despite this, the manual says not to use the included Type 27 guard for cut-off applications.

It appears that there's a lot of conflicting information as to what can and can't be done. Or rather, what should or shouldn't be done. But for everyone wondering if this grinder is suitable for cutting, the answer is yes. Buy it, you'll be happy. It's inexpensive, and if you burn it out, just buy another. It'll still be less expensive than some of the other higher-end models out there. You'll be happy.I mean really! I was so confused when I read some of these reviews about how the manual states you can't use this grinder for cutting!

TLDR: YOU MOST CERTAINLY CAN USE THIS GRINDER FOR CUTTING.

Long story is this is considered Bosh's budget friendly model so it comes without a case or the fancy vibration reducing handle, and it also comes with there most basic guard FOR the included wheel. They thoughtfully included a Type 27 grinding disk to get you started. Bosh used to make a proper sized cutting guard for this grinder but for whatever reason no longer do, so instead of offering you the parts that were intended for the device they just rewrite the user manual to coverup there shortcomings. But as you can see from the pictures I've included it's really easy to use your newly purchased grinder to make the necessary modifications. I personally like to use a Type 41 cutting wheel with the offset hub but I find it difficult to find the good diamond wheels like that. Usually they are a Type 1 flat disk which puts it much closer to the guard. I tried to allow enough guard to be left to still allow me to use it for a Type 27 grinding wheel so I don't need to have multiple guards for multiple wheels. I do occasionally use wire cones but use them without a guard and if and when I get a flat wire wheel I will cross that bridge when I come to it but don't expect too much if an issue.

I personally like to use my tools with the guards but I like the guards to stay out of my way as well. I find this is an easy fix to the problem and a fun first project as well. Instructions!? Lol

PS I did all the work you see with the Denali grinder in the background as like I said I like to work WITH guards. 😉 I would recommend both grinders for the price to anyone who is looking.Handles well and plenty of power. Used with diamond blade for cutting stone backsplash with no problems at all.If you’re wondering if this small grinder is powerful enough, it definitely is. I can’t even imagine needing a more powerful motor than this 7.5 amp one on this grinder.

It Grinds AND CUTS with a cutoff wheel excellently. The motor is more quiet and smoother than other grinders I have used in the past.

I love how ergonomic it is. It’s pretty slender and fits in your hand well. It feels solid and high quality, yet isn’t too heavy to hold onto for a long time. I can’t believe how inexpensive this one is. It’s worth its weight in gold.

JUST BUY IT, you won’t regret it!!ExcelenteI. Am. An. Idiot.

I started an earlier review talking about how I'm a professional furniture maker (bona fides/credibility, right?) who has owned many grinders over the years and while I love this grinder, I couldn't get the inner flange off... either because the machining tolerances were too tight, or there was some burr, or it just otherwise decided to fuse itself on. I even tried to use a gear puller to get it off!!! I had my return all set and figured I'd just get a replacement and make sure I reamed out the flange before seating it.

Then I had a horrible thought... and searched "flange" among the other reviews. (Major face palm). Yes. This Bosch grinder is different from all the other grinders I've owned in that the inner flange is also threaded... and, I totally forgot that. What a dummy. Now I feel so bad for all the abuse I subjected this beautiful little machine to.

Here's the highlights from my previous review:

I like having at least 3-4 grinders set up at all times with different discs so I never have to switch mid-job. My wrists have started to get pretty sore by the end of the day, so I wanted to find the lightest grinder possible -esp. for careful detail work. My go-to grinders have always been Makitas but I thought this Bosch was worth a try. Immediately, I was impressed with the design and quality. The machining and finish of all the parts looked great and it felt great to use. Grinders seem like they should be the same -it's just a motor with a threaded shaft, but compared to a crappy Metabo I wasted money on, this Bosch ran like butter... so smooth, hardly any vibration... very well balanced and lightweight... seriously, a pleasure. I imagine eventually replacing all of my grinders with this model.

Anyway... I heartily recommend this grinder, just don't forget about the threaded flange. And, the only other comment I'll make is -the cord is kinda wimpy... it's like the strength of a licorice rope... so, just make sure no off-cuts fall on it... that's all I'll say about that... otherwise... it's a great small grinder.This is a minor complaint, but I wish they would show the spindle size in this listing. I purchased a grinding wheel and it doesn't fit this grinder because the hole isn't large enough. Absolutely not a big deal but I don't understand why the spindle size isn't depicted somewhere in this listing.Mills right for a living

Picked up my first one at a thrift store for $ 20, fell in love with it after about a weeks use. (I've had old style black&decker/dewalt paddle grinders for years, rebuilt them so many times that I bought out the last of the available parts from ereplacementparts.com. )

After my last remaining grinder died and with no repair parts left available I picked up the bosch.
Its thinner than most grinders which makes it easier on your hand/forearm during long term usage for doing light duty detailing/deburring operations.

Its a locking side switch unit (which cuts it out of a lot of field usage - MSHA/OSHA thing) and has a good balance.

Its become my goto grinder for light duty work (80% of my grinding) drawback, I do mean light duty work (leaned into it too hard with a 6" cutting disc and smoked it, bought a replacement)

Currently, I have a three grinder stack on my rig, this Bosch, a 13amp Milwaukee 5" for medium duty work, and an old aluminum body black&decker 6" that refuses to die and handles everything you can throw at it (plus enough spare parts to handle cord/bearing&brush needs for quite awhile.

Hope this helps

JeffI checked out a lot of angle grinders from different manufacturers, my need being mostly DIY projects. I needed something that is fairly good quality, is good budget wise, should be easy to hold, not too heavy and easy to maneuver. Also it needed to be able to stay on without having to keep some paddle switch pressed continuously. So it came down to a choice between the Bosch 1735A (which seems shorter in length in the picture) and this one. This GWS8-45 is so slender that my thumb can almost touch my middle finger holding it so superb to hold and use it. I went with the GWS8-45 since it has the higher 7.5 amp rating though for my use even the 6 amp rating would be sufficient and the 1375A might be even more easier to hold and maneuver. Maybe I would have gone with that if I had both to hold and compare. The blade guard on the GWS8-45 is a bit interesting to install and not too easy to change positions. You have to use the provided key to loosen the bolt and then turn it around and tighten it. However the positive qualities more than make up for this and if you are using it set to a particular position for grinding or for cutting, you won't really notice it once set.I initially bought this angle grinder so that I could remove an old-school basketball goal. Back in the day, people had to rig their own, as they couldn't just buy from the store. The previous homeowner had, decades ago, installed said goal with a big ol' steel pipe. The plywood that made up the actual goal was rotted to the point that I worried a stiff breeze would blow it right down onto my wife's car, so I bought the appropriate tool for the job and got to work.

Bosch does good work for a good price. This is a basic angle grinder that will let you use those thin cutting wheels. The included wrench makes wheel swapping quick and easy. There's an appropriate guard, and a handle, for safety purposes. (You can change the handle to the other side so that, if you're left handed or approaching from that side, you have a good grip.)

This tool has helped me not just with the stupid basketball goal that needed to come down, but a few other things as well. I've used it, without problem, to break down folding chairs so that they'll fit in recycling bins. My neighbor and I cut hardware panels for both of our fencing projects--again, no problems. This grinder is a solid tool that I'm happy to have in my garage because I never know when another use for it will come up.

You also have a power switch that you can slide all the way up for continuous grinding, which is great if you're buffing something or otherwise spending a lot of time working with the tool on.

As always, be safe. Wear both safety glasses and a face shield while working with this tool, especially if you're cutting metal. Angle grinders are no joke, so take this seriously.

DONT BUY
I used to buy these in bulk for my fabrication business, 10+ employees. Some of these last a month some are dead out of the box. Absolute garbage......I bought two in Sep 2019 to add to my older two Bosch 1380 Slim grinders. Within a year, Jun 2020, one of the GWS8-45's internal motor bearing failed causing me to have to send it off foe repair. It came back working but by Nov 2020, only a few months after being repaired, it AND the second GWS8-45 have both died again. New brushes didn't fix the problem and I don't even want to bother opening them up because I totally lost faith in the model.
The model is so similar to the old faithful 1380 Slim I'd assumed only the model number had changed but it is definitely NOT the same mode.

The two older 1380 Slim's are still running like champs after years of heavy use and presumably will continue with an occasional new set brushes.
If I can no longer find the 1380 Slim model I'll, sadly, be looking at other brands because this model GWS8-45 is not built for heavy professional use the they used to be.
Just over a year from purchase I now have two useless grinders. I can't suggest a model that may not last a full year and will certainly need replacing a year after buying.This tools advertise special angle for the handle is in the wrong position for affective work, the control button instead of being at the top front of the machine is off to the left which causes to be shut off constantly and ends up making you work in a very strange backwards facing position if you want to Keep control of the power manually.
This now two weeks later with a tool that is completely broken it's pin that retains its working ability to change heads from a grinder to a wire wheel is nonfunctional, in the picture you can see the pin head poking out through the thumb grip ...this tool lasted less than five hours. It is now just another costly paperweight, I have had Makita'is that lasted for three years !!
I will literally try everything I can to get my money back for I will try everything I can to get my money back for this useless piece of junk ..
I was literally lured in with the idea of increased ergonomics 🤧🤧I purchased this grinder new in 2020. I had a Bosch 1710 that I purchased twenty years ago for $80 and used it for metal working and just about anything you can use a grinder for. As such I was happy with Bosch. I purchased the 1375a because of the price and the Bosch name. I bought it only as a backup. Well the second time it was used it went up in flames while grinding a lip off an uneven sidewalk. I am disappointed in Bosch for putting their name on an inferior Chinese product and second of all I am disappointed in Amazon for recommending it. I very seldom buy cheap power tools. The saying for serious tool buyers is buy once, cry once. Buying a quality tool that lasts twenty years even if it costs two or three times more than a cheap tool that only lasts one year is much much better buy.Take caution when purchasing this grinder. It may be a perfectly good tool in its most basic form, but accessories that expand its range of uses are not in fact available, even though Bosch advertises them in its brochures.

Specifically, and to my mind important for safety, the manual supplied for this grinder describes accessories for cutting tools (13CG-45) a cutting guard, and (13DC-45) a dust collection attachment. These options are not available anywhere. Bosch themselves cannot provide pricing or availability detail for either of these part numbers as of January 2012. I have since confirmed with Bosch that they will not produce any of the accessories.

So, if you are looking for something that goes beyond what comes in the box, i.e. anything more than grinding functions I would recommend choosing a different model such as the Bosch 18XX family of grinders, or even a different brand. I'm rather unimpressed with Bosch for being so misleading in the way this product is promoted. Also, don't bother writing a review on the Bosch site, they don't post negative reviews. Perhaps you might want to consider another vendor, I'm getting very unimpressed now that I'm also having problems with my 1274 DVS belt sander. This is probably my last Bosch tool.It is a poorly made product. I thought bosch was reliable. After only having it for less than 2 month and it just over heated and quit.Let it cool and it still wont run. I am still waiting for bosh to get hold of me for warrinty There web site will not allow data to get a erepair or a replacement.
